See also: mandarína, mandarīnā, and mandarīna

Basque

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish mandarina.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /mandaɾina/ [mãn̪.d̪a.ɾi.na]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ina, -a
  • Hyphenation: man‧da‧ri‧na

Noun

[edit]

mandarina inan

  1. mandarin orange (fruit)

Portuguese

[edit]
A user has added this entry to requests for verification(+)
If it cannot be verified that this term meets our attestation criteria, it will be deleted. Feel free to edit this entry as normal, but do not remove {{rfv}} until the request has been resolved.

Etymology

[edit]

From mandarim, because of its color's resemblance to the robes of mandarins; spelling possibly influenced by French mandarine, itself from mandarim.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /mɐ̃.daˈɾĩ.nɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /mɐ̃.daˈɾĩ.nɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /mɐ̃.daˈɾi.na/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /mɐ̃.dɐˈɾi.nɐ/

  • Hyphenation: man‧da‧ri‧na

Noun

[edit]

mandarina f (plural mandarinas)

  1. mandarin orange (fruit of the Citrus reticulata tree)
    Synonyms: see Thesaurus:tangerina

Further reading

[edit]
  • “mandarina”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “mandarina”, in Dicionário da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisboa: Academia das Ciências de Lisboa, 2001–2026
  • “mandarina”, in Dicionário infopédia da Lingua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Porto: Porto Editora, 2003–2026
  • “mandarina”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026
  • “mandarina”, in Michaelis Dicionário Brasileiro da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), São Paulo: Editora Melhoramentos, 2015–2026, →ISBN
